help_template.title: Help
help_template.addlayer_content: This tool adds a new vector layer to the map. Clicking on it opens a window in which you can enter the layer name.
help_template.selection_content: Tool for selecting elements of the layer. There are several tools that work differently if this tool is active or not.
help_template.creation_content: Tool to draw different types of geometries on the selected layer.
help_template.creation_content_1_1: Allows you to draw a point by clicking on the map.
help_template.creation_content_2_1: Allows you to create a point by entering the coordinates.
help_template.creation_content_3_1: Allows you to draw a line on the map. One click draws a point or vertex, double click finishes the drawing.
help_template.creation_content_4_1: Allows you to draw a polygon on the map. One click draws a point or vertex, double click finishes the drawing.
help_template.creation_content_5_1: Allows you to draw a regular or irregular shape on the map. One click sets the top left corner, a second click finishes the drawing.
help_template.creation_content_6_1: Allows you to write text at a point on the map.
help_template.edition_content: Tool to edit the geometries of the layer elements.
help_template.edition_content_1_1: Allows you to edit the vertices of a geometry
help_template.edition_content_2_1: Allows you to create a hole in an element. Only valid for polygons.
help_template.edition_content_3_1: Allows you to rotate the selected elements.
help_template.edition_content_5_1: Allows you to move the selected elements.
help_template.edition_content_6_1: Allows you to edit the attributes of the layer or selected elements.
help_template.edition_content_7_1: Allows you to delete all elements of the layer.
help_template.style_content: Tool to edit the styles of the layer or selected elements. They are divided into styles for point, line or polygon.
help_template.analysis_content_1_1: Allows you to display a graph that represents the relief of the terrain. In the case of specific elements, only their height and coordinates are indicated.
help_template.analysis_content_2_1: Allows you to draw an area of influence of an element.
help_template.analysis_content_3_1: Allows you to show the extension of a geographical object.
help_template.analysis_content_4_1: Allows you to view the GeoJSON of the layer or selected elements.
help_template.turf_content: Runs Turf.js geoprocessing on the vector layers of the map. Every operation (buffer; merge, extract and exclude features; layer overlay; join attributes by location; combine polygons; measurement; centers; transformations and relations) is configured in a form in the panel, choosing for each input one or several layers and their features: all of them, only the selected ones, one selected feature or the result of a previous operation. The result is a new layer or a value. The help button of the panel explains each operation.
help_template.download_content: This tool allows you to download the complete layer or selected elements in GeoJSON, KML and Shapefile format.

textHelp.help1: Vectors management extension allows for the user to create, modify, delete, apply styles, apply spatial analysis and download vector layers.
textHelp.help2: To create a layer, the add layer button on the main panel of the extension must be selected.
textHelp.help3: Once the layer has been created, it is possible to enable the geometry edition and creation controls. The first control is the one for adding new geometries to the layer, allowing digitalize points, lines, surfaces, geometric figures and texts.
textHelp.help4: Given any layer's geometries, there are two ways of managing them: all the geometries of the layer at the same time or just the selected ones. To select the geometries, the selection control must be active. To select multiple geometries at once, the control key must be kept pressed, and the geometries will be selected on click.
textHelp.help5: The next control for editing, allows to modify the existing geometries in a vector layer. In this control it is possible to modify the geometry's vertices:
textHelp.help8: scale geometries. There are some keyboard shortcuts for this action. The control key can be kept pressed to fix a scaling point, the Shift key can be used to scale keeping the shape and if both are pressed simultaneously, the shape from a certain point is kept:
textHelp.help11: and delete geometries from a layer:
textHelp.help12: The following control from the vectors management panel is for applying styles to the geometries. From this control, color, fill, opacity, width, font family for texts, font color, text to be shown and radius for point geometries can be defined.
textHelp.help13: The analysis control allows to execute an spatial analysis of the available layer's geometries. Among them, the topographic profile options:
textHelp.help16: and showing the geometries in plain text as a json format
textHelp.help17: Finally, the last control allows to download the layer in various formats: GeoJSON, KML, GPX y SHP

textHelp.help19: A use case for its parameters can be found in:

help.selections: With the selection tool, what you select in each layer is saved to be used as "Only the selected ones" or "One selected feature". Selecting in another layer does not delete these selections, and neither does clearing the selection on the map: remove them in the panel summary.
help.ops: They are all configured in a form in this panel, which does not block the map: for each input you choose one or several layers and which features of each one to use. When it opens, the first input uses the active layer (its selection, if the selection tool is active). The result is a new layer or a value; the source layers are not modified.

scopes.selection: the features of its saved selection.
scopes.feature: a single feature of its saved selection, chosen from a list. Use it to compare or measure two features, also of the same layer.
scopes.result: a layer created by a previous operation, to chain operations.

help.layerOutput: A new layer with the legend "Turf: <operation> (n)", which can be used as the input of other operations ("Result of a previous operation"). The form lets you choose the fields that are copied and whether capa_origen is added.
help.valueOutput: A value shown in a message; no layer is created.
help.combinedOutput: When several features make up a single result, num_entidades is added with how many there are. Their fields are only copied if you choose them, and their values are combined according to "Values of the combined fields": the value of an arbitrary feature is never taken.

categoriesDesc.proximity: Creates areas within a distance of the features of a layer.
categoriesDesc.extraction: They copy whole features to a new layer without changing their geometries: they merge features of several layers, extract a selection, exclude features or extract the ones that meet a spatial relation.
categoriesDesc.overlay: Computes new geometries from how two layers overlap, with the fields of both.
categoriesDesc.join: Adds to each feature the fields of the related features of another layer, without changing its geometry.
categoriesDesc.measurement: Area, length, distance, extent and a point at a distance along a line, with features of one or several layers.
categoriesDesc.center: Center, centroid, center of mass or a point on each feature, with its fields.
categoriesDesc.transformation: Simplify, hulls, smooth lines, rotate, scale and translate, with features of one or several layers.
categoriesDesc.combine: They create a new geometry from polygons of one or several layers: they merge them, compute their common area or subtract some from others. Their fields are combined.
categoriesDesc.relation: They check the relation between two features, of the same layer or of different layers.

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.desc: Creates a polygon at the given distance around each feature, with its fields, or a single polygon with every area dissolved.

input.label: Input features
input.help: Points, lines or polygons of one or several layers.

mergeFeatures.name: Merge or extract features
mergeFeatures.desc: Copies to a new layer the chosen features of one or several layers (all of them, only the selected ones, one of them or a previous result) without changing their geometries or fields. Fields with the same name share a column.

input.label: Features to copy
input.help: Add several layers to merge them into one; choose "Only the selected ones" to extract a selection.

excludeFeatures.name: Exclude features
excludeFeatures.desc: Copies to a new layer the starting features except the excluded ones. It compares which features they are (their layer and position), not their geometries: it does not subtract areas.

input.label: Starting features
input.help: By default, every feature of the active layer. You can add several layers.

exclude.label: Features to exclude
exclude.help: By default, the saved selection of the active layer. Only the ones that are also starting features are removed.

extractByLocation.name: Extract by location
extractByLocation.desc: Copies to a new layer, whole and unclipped, the input features that meet the spatial relation with the condition features.

input.label: Features to extract from
input.help: They are copied with their original geometry. You can add several layers.

condition.label: Features that define the condition
condition.help: The relation must hold with at least one of them (with "Disjoint", with none). You can add several layers.

layerIntersection.name: Layer intersection
layerIntersection.desc: Creates the common part of each input feature with each overlay polygon that crosses it, with the fields of both. Points and lines are clipped and keep their type.

input.label: Input features
input.help: Points, lines or polygons to clip. You can add several layers.

overlay.label: Overlay polygons
overlay.help: Polygons to clip with. You can add several layers.

layerUnion.name: Layer union
layerUnion.desc: Splits the polygons of both inputs into the parts where they overlap and where they do not, like the QGIS union. Each part carries the fields of the features covering it and empty fields for the other input. It is not a dissolve.

input.label: First input
input.help: Polygons of one or several layers. Overlaps between its own features are not split.

overlay.label: Second input
overlay.help: Polygons of one or several layers. Overlaps between its own features are not split.

layerDifference.name: Layer difference
layerDifference.desc: Creates the part of each input feature outside the subtracted polygons, with its fields.

input.label: Input features
input.help: Points, lines or polygons to subtract from. You can add several layers.

spatialJoin.name: Join attributes by location (spatial join)
spatialJoin.desc: Copies the target features without changing their geometry and adds the fields of the join features they meet the spatial relation with.

target.label: Features whose geometries are kept
target.help: Each feature keeps its geometry and its fields. You can add several layers.

join.label: Features that provide the fields
join.help: Their fields are added to the related features. If you add several layers, their fields with the same name share a column.

union.name: Merge polygons (union)
union.desc: Merges the chosen polygons of one or several layers into a single geometry and removes their inner boundaries. Separate polygons make up a multipart geometry or, if requested, one feature each. It does not copy features or split layers.

input.label: Polygons to merge
input.help: Of one or several layers: one feature, only the selected ones, all of them or a previous result.

intersect.name: Common area of the polygons (intersection)
intersect.desc: Creates the area shared by all the chosen polygons, of one or several layers. If they have no common area, no layer is created.

input.label: Polygons
input.help: At least two, of one or several layers.

difference.name: Subtract polygons (difference)
difference.desc: Creates the area of the starting polygons (merged) not covered by the subtracted polygons. With two or more polygons selected in the active layer, it subtracts the others from the first one, as before.

input.label: Starting polygons
input.help: By default, the first selected feature of the active layer. You can add several layers.

overlay.label: Polygons to subtract
overlay.help: By default, the selection of the active layer. Features that are also starting polygons are not subtracted.

area.name: Area
area.desc: Adds up the area of the chosen polygons, of one or several layers. Overlapping areas are counted once per polygon.

input.label: Polygons
input.help: Of one or several layers; features that are not polygons are skipped.

length.name: Length
length.desc: Adds up the length of the chosen lines, of one or several layers.

input.label: Lines
input.help: Of one or several layers; features that are not lines are skipped.

distance.name: Distance
distance.desc: Calculates the distance between two points, of the same layer or of different layers.

first.label: Origin point
first.help: A single point. By default, the first selected feature of the active layer.

second.label: Destination point
second.help: A single point. By default, the second selected feature of the active layer or the one of another saved selection.

bbox.name: Extent (bbox)
bbox.desc: Calculates the extent (bounding box) of the chosen features, of one or several layers, in EPSG:4326.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

along.name: Point along line
along.desc: Creates on each line a point at the given distance from its start, with the fields of the line.

input.label: Lines
input.help: LineStrings of one or several layers; multilines are skipped.

center.name: Center
center.desc: Creates the center of the extent of each feature, with its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

centroid.name: Centroid
centroid.desc: Creates the centroid (mean of the vertices) of each feature, with its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

centerOfMass.name: Center of mass
centerOfMass.desc: Creates the center of mass of each feature, with its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

pointOnFeature.name: Point on feature
pointOnFeature.desc: Creates a point that is always on each feature, with its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

simplify.name: Simplify
simplify.desc: Simplifies each line and polygon (Douglas-Peucker algorithm) and keeps its fields.

input.label: Lines and polygons
input.help: Of one or several layers; points are skipped.

convex.name: Convex hull
convex.desc: Creates the smallest convex polygon that contains all the chosen features, of one or several layers.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

envelope.name: Envelope
envelope.desc: Creates the rectangle that contains all the chosen features, of one or several layers.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

bezierSpline.name: Smooth line (Bézier)
bezierSpline.desc: Turns each line into a smoothed Bézier curve and keeps its fields.

input.label: Lines
input.help: LineStrings of one or several layers; multilines are skipped.

transformRotate.name: Rotate
transformRotate.desc: Rotates each feature around its centroid or around a common pivot and keeps its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

transformScale.name: Scale
transformScale.desc: Scales each feature from an origin point and keeps its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

transformTranslate.name: Translate
transformTranslate.desc: Moves each feature a distance in a direction and keeps its fields.

input.label: Features
input.help: Of one or several layers.

booleanPointInPolygon.name: Point in polygon
booleanPointInPolygon.desc: Checks whether a point is inside a polygon, of the same layer or of different layers.

first.label: Point
first.help: A single point. By default, the first selected feature of the active layer.

second.label: Polygon
second.help: A single polygon. By default, the second selected feature of the active layer or the one of another saved selection.

booleanIntersects.name: Intersect
booleanIntersects.desc: Checks whether two features, of the same layer or of different layers, touch or cross.

first.label: First feature
first.help: A single feature. By default, the first selected one of the active layer.

second.label: Second feature
second.help: A single feature. By default, the second selected one of the active layer or the one of another saved selection.

booleanContains.name: Contains
booleanContains.desc: Checks whether the first feature contains the second one, of the same layer or of different layers.

first.label: Containing feature
first.help: A single feature. By default, the first selected one of the active layer.

second.label: Contained feature
second.help: A single feature. By default, the second selected one of the active layer or the one of another saved selection.

booleanWithin.name: Within
booleanWithin.desc: Checks whether the first feature is inside the second one, of the same layer or of different layers.

first.label: Feature inside
first.help: A single feature. By default, the first selected one of the active layer.

second.label: Containing feature
second.help: A single feature. By default, the second selected one of the active layer or the one of another saved selection.

params.separateParts: One feature for each separate part

paramsHelp.radius: Buffer distance. A negative value shrinks the polygons.
paramsHelp.concavity: Empty: convex hull. The lower it is (minimum 1), the closer it fits the features.
paramsHelp.pivot: In degrees (EPSG:4326). Leave both empty to rotate each feature around its centroid.
paramsHelp.dissolve: Merges every area into a single feature; their fields are combined.
paramsHelp.predicateExtract: Relation of each input feature with the condition features. "Within" requires it to be inside: touching the boundary is not enough.
paramsHelp.predicateJoin: "Within": the target feature is inside the join feature. "Contains": the target feature contains the join feature.
paramsHelp.matchPolicy: "One feature per match" repeats the target feature for each related feature. "Largest overlap" picks the one with the largest common area or length; on a tie, the first one in the layer.
paramsHelp.keepUnmatched: If unchecked, features without any match are not copied.
paramsHelp.separateParts: If the merged polygons form separate areas, creates one feature per area, with the fields of the features it is made of. If unchecked, creates a single multipart geometry.
paramsHelp.fieldPolicy: "Distinct values" gathers the distinct values of the features, separated by commas. "Common value" copies the value only if every feature shares it; otherwise it is left empty.
paramsHelp.sourceLayer: Adds a column with the name of the layer each feature comes from (or the layers, if the result combines several).
